Elliot vocabulary | iso3 = xbb | linglist = xbb | aiatsis = E61 | aiatsisname = Bindal | glotto = bind1234 | glottoname = Cunningham list | glottorefname = Bindal-Cunningham | glotto2 = bind1235 | glottoname2 = Gorton list | glottorefname2 = Bindal-Gorton | glotto3 = bind1236 | glottoname3 = Mount Elliot list | glottorefname3 = Bindal-Mount Elliot | map = Lower Burdekin languages.png | mapcaption = Lower Burdekin languages (green) among other Pama–Nyungan (tan) | states = [[Australia]] | acceptance = geographic | altname = [[Bindal language|Bindal]] ? }} [[File:BurdekinRiver1.jpg|250px|thumb|The Burdekin River in 2005]] The '''Lower Burdekin languages''' are a geographical grouping of three distinct [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Aboriginal languages]],{{Cite web |title=2009-014 {{!}} ISO 639-3 |url=https://iso639-3.sil.org/request/2009-014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190704084701/https://iso639-3.sil.org/request/2009-014 |archive-date=2019-07-04 |access-date=2025-02-27 |website=iso639-3.sil.org |url-status=live |language=en}} spoken around the mouth of the [[Burdekin River]] in north [[Queensland]]. One short wordlist in each was collected in the 19th century, and published in the second volume of ''[[The Australian Race]]'' in 1886.{{cite book |last1=Curr |first1=Edward Micklethwaite |author-link=Edward Micklethwaite Curr |title=The Australian race: its origin, languages, customs, place of landing in Australia and the routes by which it spread itself over the continent |date=1886 |volume=2 |publisher=Government Printer |location=Melbourne |language=en |url=https://archive.org/details/cu31924026093827}} These languages have since gone [[language death|extinct]], with no more having been recorded. Due to the paucity of the available data, almost nothing of their [[grammar|grammatical structure]] is known. The three languages may have been [[Maric languages|Maric]]. However, Breen analysed two of the lists and concluded that they were different languages, neither Maric. He presumes that one of them was [[Bindal language|Bindal]].{{cite web |title=E61: Bindal |work=Australian Indigenous Languages Database |date=26 July 2019 |publisher=[[Australian Institute of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander Studies]] |url=https://collection.aiatsis.gov.au/austlang/language/E61 |access-date=25 November 2020}} == Wordlist == {| class="wikitable sortable" !
